prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the vertical distance gradient from the head-mounted camera down toward the ground, showing the camera wearer's own chest and shoulders brightest at the bottom (~0.2–0.4 m away, facing forward away from the camera), the arms and gripped lawn mower handlebar within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m), the mower's grass catcher bag and partly cut-off front engine deck ahead (~0.9–1.5 m), and the ground plane below (~1.5–1.8 m). Across the five frames, the arms and handlebar shift slightly farther and darker (~0.7–0.8 m) as the wearer pushes the mower forward in frame 3, then become much brighter (~0.4–0.5 m) and occlude the lower legs in frames 4 and 5 as the wearer pulls the handle in against the torso while executing a 180-degree turn. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the suspended handlebar, thin side struts, the wearer's stepping right leg in frame 2 (~0.9–1.2 m), and the raised bushes on the right in frame 4 (~1.0–1.3 m) from the flat grass and dark cast shadows directly beneath them. However, the map is unreliable along the upper-left pavement and pebble border where the flat ground drops off to near-black, and on the wearer's chest in frames 4 and 5 where white saturation obscures the depth boundary between the shirt, hands, and handlebar.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map labels the camera wearer in the lower foreground of all five frames as a `person` (pink mask covering the upper torso and arms at ~0.2–0.8 m from the camera, facing forward with the lower body largely occluded by the chest), while no other people are actually present in the scene. Across the sequence, the pink mask tracks the wearer's arms extending forward with the handlebar in frame 3 (~0.7–0.8 m) and pulling back against the chest during the turn in frames 4 and 5 (~0.4–0.5 m), where the torso fills the lower frame and partially occludes the hands and control bar. Although the masks cleanly separate the contours of the wearer's torso, arms, and held grip from the textured grass, pebbles, and shadows below, the object classifications are highly unreliable from this top-down egocentric angle. The model completely misses the lawn mower (~0.9–1.5 m ahead), misclassifies the grey center control grip between the wearer's hands (~0.5–0.8 m away) as a `cell phone` in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, and hallucinates extra `person` masks on the mower bag and grass shadow in frame 2 (cyan mask at ~0.8–1.5 m) and at the bottom edge of frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's left and right hands gripping the mower handlebar within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m in front of and below the camera) in frames 1 through 3, showing the fingers curled around the grips as the hands push forward from ~0.6 m in frames 1–2 to ~0.8 m in frame 3. In frames 4 and 5, as the wearer turns around and pulls the handlebar tight against the chest (~0.4–0.5 m), the hands become partially occluded by the torso and the map fails to detect either hand. While the magenta keypoints in frames 1–3 make the exact wrist angles and finger placements on the control bar easier to read than in the sunlit RGB frames, the map completely misses the camera wearer's own body skeleton (~0.2–1.5 m below the camera) across all five frames due to extreme top-down foreshortening. Furthermore, the pose estimator is severely unreliable on the lawn mower in frames 1 and 5, hallucinating a yellow body skeleton (~0.5–1.5 m away) that misinterprets the red mower engine at the top as a head facing the camera, the grass bag and frame struts as a torso, and the lower handlebar struts as bent legs.
